newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures fall after U.S. payrolls data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures fall after U.S. payrolls data.

text.p: U.S. debt futures were moderately lower and near the morning's low hit after stronger-than-forecast U.S. July jobs figures.
Nonfarm payrolls rose 316,000 versus average forecasts for a 193,000-job increase. June's original 217,000 payrolls increase was revised upward to 228,000.
July's jobless rate fell to 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent in June and against forecasts for 4.9 percent.
Average hourly earnings last month stayed unchanged at $12.23. Traders had expected a 0.2-percent rise. Average weekly hours fell to 34.4, and overtime hours fell to 4.6.
Manufacturing jobs in July fell 5,000, while services and government jobs increased 113,000 and 56,000, respectively.
The Labor department said, however, that the government jobs growth may reflect problematic seasonal adjustments.
June U.S. personal income rose 0.6 pct and spending rose 0.3 percent against forecasts for 0.4-percent gain in each.

The market also faces a slew of other economic data Friday, among them the July national purchasing manager's index, the final July University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey, and June U.S. factory orders.
Floor brokers and analysts said the data did not reveal enough strength or worrisome inflation to instill fear that the Federal Reserve would need to hike interest rates soon.

The report, which showed "continuing labor market tightness and unbelievably benign wage inflation," likely will leave the Fed on hold, said John Nyhoff, chief economist, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Futures (USA) Inc.
"The average hourly earnings certainly forces them to do nothing this month and maybe next month," Nyhoff added.
But he also waited to see national purchasers price data, due at 0900 CDT, after Thursday's strong Chicago price data.
"One month doesn't change the market," said a Treasury bond futures floor broker when asked if the report meant the Fed would tighten credit. "We're keying off the unchanged hourly earnings."

Despite the early spike down, September Treasury bond futures held Thursday's low at 116-04/32 early Friday, brokers noted. It matched Thursday's peak at 116-31/32 near the opening bell, thus far forming an inside range day.

At 0847 CDT/1347 GMT, Sept T-bond lost 14/32 to 116-10/32, note off 10/32 at 110-22/32, munis fell 11/32 to 121-26/32, Dec euros off 0.020 to 94.195, Dec bills off 0.65 at 94.840. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
